finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches an attacker-supplied URL with no validation, so it is a full SSRF. An attacker can reach internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) and localhost. The first 500 bytes of the response body are returned to the caller.

trace.note: target = request.args.get('url', '') takes the query parameter directly
requests.get(target) is called with the unvalidated URL. Redirects are followed by default.
resp.status_code and resp.text[:500] are returned to the attacker, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist or denylist. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check used in /partner is not applied here. No private-IP or metadata blocking, and no redirect restriction. The 5s timeout and 500-byte truncation limit the output but do not prevent access.

verdict.reason: app.py:15 reads the attacker-controlled `url` query parameter and app.py:16 passes it to requests.get with no host or scheme validation, while app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 bytes of the body; the ALLOWED_HOSTS check exists only in /partner (app.py:23-25), and app.py is the only file, so there is no middleware or auth.
